title: Book 9 — Calliope, Chapter 13
paragraphs: Having said this, he departed and went back; and Mardonius was no longer at all eager to remain in Attica when he heard the message. Before he was informed of this, he had been waiting because he wanted the Athenians' news of what they were about to do, and he had not been injuring or laying waste the land of Attica, because he kept hoping they would make a treaty with him. When he failed to persuade them, and was now informed of everything, he began to withdraw from the country before Pausanias's force arrived at the Isthmus — having first set fire to Athens and torn down and destroyed whatever was left standing of the walls, houses, or temples. He marched away for this reason: first, because Attica was not a land where cavalry could operate freely, and also because if he were defeated in battle in Attica, there was no way of retreat except through a narrow pass, so that a few men could block them. He intended, therefore, to retreat to Thebes and fight near a friendly city and in country where cavalry could operate freely.
